title: The EM Wave Bench
summary: Find E and B, their directions, wavelength, wave number and energy density of an electromagnetic wave.
subject: physics
concepts: E × B along the direction of travel
Equal energy in E and B
learningOutcome: The student can find the amplitude and direction of E and B in a plane wave, the wavelength, wave number and frequency, read a wave equation, and show that the two fields carry equal energy.

levels.title: E and B
levels.adds: Baseline: in vacuum E₀ = cB₀, in phase (Ex 8.7, Example 8.1).
hints: E = cB in vacuum, with c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s.
The fields rise and fall together.

levels.title: Which way is B?
levels.adds: New idea: the wave is transverse, and E × B points along the direction of travel (Ex 8.4).
hints: B is at right angles to both E and the direction of travel.
E × B must point the way the wave moves.
Try the right-hand rule for E × B with each choice.

levels.title: Wavelengths
levels.adds: New idea: λ = c/f for any frequency (Ex 8.4, 8.5, 8.6).
hints: λ = c/f, with f in hertz.

levels.title: A plane wave
levels.adds: More steps: from E₀ and f find B₀, k and λ (Ex 8.8).

levels.title: Read the equation
levels.adds: More steps: read k and ω from B = B₀ sin(kx + ωt) (Example 8.2).
hints: The coefficient of x is k = 2π/λ.
The coefficient of t is ω = 2πf.

levels.title: Energy in the fields
levels.adds: More steps: the average energy densities of E and B are equal (Ex 8.10).
hints: The average magnetic energy density is B₀²/4μ₀.

misconceptions: The electric and magnetic fields of a wave are out of phase
Most of the energy of a wave is in its electric field
